Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Apex Medical Devices Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are David Larson, CEO; Robert Kline, CFO; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Jennifer Brooks, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Larson.

David Larson:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Medical Devices demonstrated significant progress this quarter, driven by our focus on innovation, operational excellence, and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover seven key aspects of our performance:
1. Gross margin trends and supply chain commentary
2. Organic revenue growth by segment and geography
3. Capital equipment vs consumables mix trends
4. Inventory management and working capital optimization
5. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
6. Procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary
7. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress

Robert will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Dr. Vasquez will offer insights into our technology roadmap, and Jennifer will discuss our commercial strategies. Afterwards, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with gross margin trends and supply chain commentary. Our GAAP gross margin expanded 210 basis points year-over-year to 67.2% this quarter, the strongest quarterly figure in our history and our fifth straight quarter of sequential gains. Adjusted for one-time ERP charges, it hit 68.1%, surpassing our guidance of 66-67%. This stems from multi-year efforts across product mix, pricing, and cost efficiencies.

Product mix led with 150 basis points of lift, as demand surged for high-margin structural heart items like our next-gen TAVR valves, reminiscent of Medtronic's CoreValve, and premium robotic systems similar to Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci. These, with margins over 75%, made up 28% of revenue, up from 22% last year. Electrophysiology shone, with our Watchman FLX-like LAA closure device up 18% on expanded indications and CMS APC reimbursement.

Pricing added 80 basis points, holding ASPs steady on disposables like catheters and neuromodulation leads despite U.S. hospital pressures. We raised list prices 3-5% on select items in new Vizient and Premier GPO deals, staying competitive with Boston Scientific and Abbott.

COGS improved 130 basis points via manufacturing gains and supply chain improvements. Input inflation eased to 1.2% from 2023's 4-5% peaks, with stable resin prices for orthopedic implants and balloon catheters.

By region, U.S. margins hit 69.5% at 52% of revenue, aided by 92% utilization at Galway and Plymouth sites. Europe improved to 65.8% despite euro FX headwinds, thanks to MDR tailwinds. APAC reached 70.2% on premium sales in China with Mindray and neurovascular ramps in Japan.

On supply chain, we've diversified since 2022 shortages—no supplier over 15% of critical materials, down from 25%. Dual-sourcing PEBAX and polycarbonate avoids Red Sea issues. We've spent $150 million on Industry 4.0, with AI forecasting at Heredia cutting inventory to 145 days and boosting extrusion throughput 22%. EtO expansion in Memphis provides 20% excess sterilization capacity.

We're insourcing ICD leads for 30% savings by 2026, nearshoring 65% to Mexico, and locking 70% of 2025-2027 volumes with inflation-linked deals from Dow and TSMC. Q3 guidance: 67.5-68.5%, full-year adjusted 67.8% with 250 bps expansion. This positions us as a margin leader at 18x EV/EBITDA.

Now, let's talk about organic revenue growth by segment and geography. Excluding our NeuroStim tuck-in and FX, we posted 9.2% organic growth, up from 7.8% in Q2 and sixth quarter of double-digit constant currency in cores. Procedural recovery to 95% pre-COVID, premium mix, and 1-2% ASP gains drove this.

By segment, Cardiovascular at 32% of revenue grew 12.5%, with TAVR up 15% and our OmniFlow valve gaining 2.2 share points to 28% per Millennium. Coronary interventions rose 8% on EchoStent's bioresorbable tech. Orthopedics & Spine, 25%, hit 7.8% with 10% hips/knees volumes at 105% of 2019; PrecisionNav 3.0 drove 40% knee mix. MedSurg & Endoscopy, 27%, grew 8.9% led by 22% single-use scopes. Diabetes & Neuromodulation, 16%, up 11.2% with 14% CGM and 9% SCS. Diagnostics & Monitoring, 14%, at 6.4%.

Geographically, U.S. 10.8% at 58% share on elective demand and IDN wins. EMEA 8.1%, strong in Germany/UK TAVR. APAC 7.5%, China 5% post-NRDL, Japan/Australia 12%/11%. Emerging 12.2% led by Brazil/India.

Our framework—innovate, penetrate, expand—with $450M YTD R&D and 18 launches, grew share 80 bps. Q4 outlook 9-11%, full-year 9% organic, 12% EPS.

Moving on to capital equipment vs consumables mix trends. Consumables hit 73% of our $1.28 billion revenue, up from 68%, with 82% margins vs 52% for capital at 27%. This annuity shift drove 420 bps overall margin gain.

Capital deleveraged 600 bps on hospital capex caution; CoreFlex base grew 22% to 4,200 units, pull-through $1.45M annualized, up 11% at 18.5 procedures/week. U.S. 78% consumables mix, EMEA 70%, APAC 65%.

Drivers: single-use conversion 40% in endoscopy, AI utilization in CoreFlex, sustainable bio-plastics adding $45M. Targeting 80/20 by FY2026 with RCT data. Q4 consumables 20-22% growth.

Next, inventory management and working capital optimization. DIO fell to 92 days, down 18% YoY, turns to 4.0x vs industry 3.5x, CCC to 68 days—best in class. Freed $187M, funding R&D.

U.S. ortho 85 days with VMI, Europe 78 via Leipzig hub, APAC 110. SAP S/4HANA with IoT/RFID cut write-offs 42%; ML forecasting at 93% accuracy. DPO to 72 days, $250M for M&A. Year-end DIO 85 days supporting 12-15% growth, 210 bps gross margin lift.

Then, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains. SG&A at $285M, down 8% YoY, 28.2% of revenue—380 bps better, $52M savings to 24.8% op margin.

Sales/marketing down 10% on rep productivity to $4.2M/revenue via MedRep AI, 1,850 reps. G&A down 4% on VendorSync $18M, ZBB $12M. ERP automated 40%, ProcureAI 11% savings, Hyderabad 25% cheaper.

U.S. 26.5%, Europe 32% offset by wins, APAC 24%. Reinvesting in robotics, $1.2B cash for M&A. Q4 27.5-28.5%, $180M full-year savings.

Procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary. Volumes up 13% globally, ahead of market, 18% stacked vs 2021. Ortho 16%, structural heart 11% with TAVR 19%, neuromod 25%.

U.S. 15%, Europe 10%, China/APAC 8%, emerging 20%. Digital integration, supply resilience, reimbursement tailwinds. Q3 12-14%, full-year 13-15% organic.

Finally, R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress. We invested $285M, 14.2% of $2.01B revenue, up 11% YoY, toward 14-15% full-year. Mix: 45% cardio, 28% neuro/diabetes, etc. Six milestones: Evolut PRO+ TAVR PULSE trial success, FDA IDE; Percept PC INSIGHT interim; MiniMed 870G FDA approval, 15K units; Hugo RAS first-in-human; Mako 2.0 FORM trial.

U.S. Breakthroughs, Europe MDR, Asia approvals. Megatrends: outpatient, AI/ML, sustainability. M&A like NeuroPace. $3.5-4B peak sales.

I will now turn the call over to Robert for a review of our financial results.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, David. As David highlighted, we achieved strong financial results this quarter. Total revenue reached $2.01 billion, up 14% reported and 16% constant currency, driven by the trends outlined. Adjusted EPS grew 15% to $1.85, beating guidance. Operating margins expanded to 24.8%, with full-year outlook for 9% organic growth, 67.8% gross margins, and EPS of $7.40-$7.60. Expenses controlled tightly, cash flow $1.2 billion YTD. We're raising full-year guidance across the board.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Vasquez for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Robert. We continue to invest in cutting-edge technologies. Our development of next-gen TAVR and robotic systems like Hugo RAS is progressing well, and we anticipate they will revolutionize structural heart and minimally invasive surgery. Building on the R&D progress David noted, we're advancing 24 programs, with key trials like PULSE and INSIGHT on track for approvals, enhancing precision and outcomes in cardio and neuro.

Next, Jennifer with some insights on our commercial strategy.

Jennifer Brooks:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. Our commercial team has been instrumental in driving adoption of our products. We are focused on expanding our market presence and enhancing customer engagement. Key wins include IDN contracts with Kaiser and HCA, GPO expansions with Vizient, and APAC partnerships like Mindray, boosting share in TAVR, robotics, and CGM. Procedure growth and premium mix penetration remain priorities, with digital tools aiding surgeon adoption.

Now, back to David for Q&A.

David Larson:
Thank you, Jennifer. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On gross margins, can you expand on supply chain risks like nitrosamines or Taiwan tensions, and how you're mitigating?

David Larson:
Great question, Alex. We've built resilience with diversification—no single supplier over 15%—and vertical integration like insourcing leads. For nitrosamines, rigorous testing exceeds FDA thresholds, and our EtO excess capacity buffers sterilization. Taiwan? Dual-sourcing silicon and nearshoring insulate us. Cash at $2.1B gives acquisition optionality.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Singh with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Priya Singh:
Hi team, strong organic growth—curious about Q4 acceleration in cardio and diabetes, any segment-specific color?

Robert Kline:
Thanks, Priya. Yes, cardio benefits from TAVR share gains and EchoStent rollout, targeting 12-14% growth. Diabetes from Liberty Patch attach rates and China NRDL, 13-15%. Overall 9-11%, with U.S. electives and APAC ramps key.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Chen:
Good morning. On consumables mix shift to 73%, how sustainable is the pull-through improvement, and capex outlook?

Jennifer Brooks:
Mike, pull-through at $1.45M is durable, driven by 18.5 procedures/week via AI analytics and single-use kits. Utilization focus and RCT evidence sustain it. Capital stabilizing 25-27% mix as hospitals utilize bases; we see modest Q4 uptick with OR budgets loosening.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Laura Patel:
Thanks. Impressive R&D progress—timeline for Percept PC PMA and impact on neuromod growth?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Laura, Q4 FY24 PMA submission on track, with INSIGHT data showing 28% tremor reduction. Builds on 25% volume surge; expect 20%+ growth in FY25, capturing opioid-sparing demand in $2.8B market.

David Larson:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are dedicated to driving innovation and delivering value to our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
